steps.content: The idea says: coins that trade more per dollar (low dollar-denominated turnover) should do better. So I want the level of dollar-denominated turnover, which is quote_volume / volume, and the idea is bullish on it. First test: the plain 20-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0071
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0103 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0215, 2023 +0.0058, 2024 +0.0092

The 20-day average of dollar-denominated turnover gives +0.0103 incremental IC with t = 3.0, and all three sub-periods are positive (+0.0215, +0.0058, +0.0092). That is already in the good range, so I stop here rather than keep tuning the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins that trade less per dollar — the low-turnover ones — do earn higher returns over the following days, and the effect is not a single-period artifact. The plain 20-day average of quote_volume over volume is the version I hand in.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('volume')).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says heavy aggressive buying (taker buy share) leaves the price to fall, so the factor should fall as the 5-day average taker buy share rises. I'll start with the simplest form: minus the 5-day average of taker_quote_vol over quote_volume.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0090 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

The simple 5-day average comes out clearly negative and consistent across all three periods (t = −3.0), so on this history heavy aggressive buying has actually been followed by gains. That is the idea's own failure; the factor stays pointing the way the idea says (higher buy share → lower factor value) and the 5-day average is what I hand in.

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says heavy aggressive buying (taker buy share) is followed by a pullback, so the factor should fall as the buy share rises — I'll put the minus sign on the outside. I'll start with the simplest form: the 20-day average of the taker buy share, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0010
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0102 (t = -3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0190, 2023 -0.0040, 2024 -0.0120

The 20-day average gives incremental IC −0.0102 with all three periods negative (t = −3.5), so on this history heavy buying is followed by *stronger* returns, the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I'll check a shorter 10-day window to see whether the 20-day level is the problem or whether the 10-day average carries the same sign.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0028
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0065 (t = -2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0159, 2023 -0.0010, 2024 -0.0074

The 10-day average is also negative (−0.0065, t = −2.2), so shortening the window does not rescue the idea. Both windows agree in sign, so the 20-day version is the one to hand in.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. After heavy aggressive buying the taker-buy share (taker_quote_vol / quote_volume) the price continued to rise, not fall, with an incremental IC of −0.0102 (t = −3.5) and the same sign in every sub-period. So the factor must point the way the idea says — heavy buying → higher number — and that direction is what I submit.

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says a surge in trade volume is bearish, so the factor should fall as the 5-day average of `num_trades` rises. I'll start with the simplest version of that: the negative of the 5-day mean of `num_trades`.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0481
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0089 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0111, 2023 +0.0106, 2024 +0.0062

The first version already gives +0.0089 with all three periods positive and t = 6.1, so the idea holds on this history. Before settling, I'll check whether a 10-day window (min_periods 8) is a better estimator of "far above normal" than 5 days, since a longer average should be less noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0452
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0065, 2023 +0.0092, 2024 +0.0052

The 10-day window drops to +0.0071, so the 5-day average is the better estimator and I'll keep it. One last check on the 20-day window (min_periods 16) to see whether even a longer average is worth it.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0025 (t = 2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0013, 2023 +0.0033, 2024 +0.0024

The 20-day average collapses to +0.0025, so 5 days is the best of the three and I'll stop here.

What I found: taking the negative of the 5-day average of `num_trades` works on this history — coins that trade far more than their own 5-day norm go on to underperform, and the effect is consistent across all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0111, 2023 +0.0106, 2024 +0.0062), with t = 6.1. The 10-day and 20-day windows both did worse, so the 5-day average is the one to hand in.

The idea says the taker buy share is bullish, so the factor should rise with it. I'll start with the simplest form: the 20-day average of taker_quote_vol over quote_volume.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0010
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0102 (t = 3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0190, 2023 +0.0040, 2024 +0.0120

The 20-day taker share gives +0.0102 with t = 3.5 and the same sign in all three periods (+0.019 / +0.004 / +0.012), so the direction holds. Now I want to check whether a shorter 10-day window is a better estimate of "currently large aggressive-buy share", since the 20-day version sits at +0.0102.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0028
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0065 (t = 2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0159, 2023 +0.0010, 2024 +0.0074

The 10-day window is clearly weaker (+0.0065, t = 2.2, and 2023 is almost flat), so the 20-day average is the better form. I'll stop here rather than keep tuning windows on the same history.

What I found: the 20-day average taker share is the best of the two, at +0.0102 with t = 3.5, and it is positive in every period (2022H2 +0.019, 2023 +0.004, 2024 +0.012), so the idea holds on this history, though the effect is modest. Shorter averaging is worse, so I hand in the 20-day version.

<factor>Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says: coins that trade more times per day do better. So the factor should rise with the number of trades, which is `num_trades` — it is already a count, so it is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form, a 20-day mean of that count.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

The 20-day average of trade count comes out at −0.0025 with the same sign in every sub-period, so on this history high-trade-volume coins did slightly worse — the effect is real but the opposite of the idea. I'll keep the idea's direction and just check whether the 20-day window is what's driving it.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0326
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0029 (t = -2.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0016, 2023 -0.0023, 2024 -0.0041

The 60-day window gives −0.0029, also negative and negative in every period — so the sign is not an artifact of the 20-day window. One more check: a 10-day average to see whether the window is what's pushing it.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0452
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0071 (t = -5.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0065, 2023 -0.0092, 2024 -0.0052

The 10-day window is the strongest of the three (−0.0071, t = −5.5, negative in every sub-period), so the effect is stable across window lengths. I stop here rather than spend the last test on the same quantity.

What I found: on this history the idea does not hold. Coins with the most trades per day went on to do slightly *worse*, and the sign is the same in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so it is not a single-period artifact. I am keeping the idea's direction as stated, so the factor rises with the trade count; the honest IC is negative, and I hand in the 20-day version since it is the simplest and least window-dependent of the three.

<factor>Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says coins that trade more per day do better, so the factor should rise with the level of daily turnover. The simplest reading is the 20-day average of quote_volume per day, which is already unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0011 (t = -1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0025, 2023 -0.0020, 2024 +0.0004

The 20-day average of quote_volume per day has an incremental IC of −0.0011 with t = −1.9, and it flips sign between 2022H2 and 2024, so on this history heavy-trade coins did slightly worse. Before concluding, I want to check whether the effect is really about the level of turnover or whether it is the *relative* level (heavy traders vs. quiet ones), which is the part not already removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0010 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0010, 2023 -0.0038, 2024 +0.0069

The relative-to-own-60-day version flips the sign to +0.0010 with t = 0.4, and 2024 is the only positive period (+0.0069), so the level of turnover is what carries the signal, not the "heavy traders vs. quiet" form. That is two tests in a row that failed to beat the best by 0.002, so I stop here and hand in the level form.

What I found: averaging quote_volume per day over 20 days gives an incremental IC of −0.0011 with t = −1.9, so on this history heavy-trade coins actually did slightly worse the next day; that is the honest reading, and I keep the idea's direction (higher turnover → higher factor) rather than flipping the sign to chase it.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says coins with more trades per day do better, so the factor should rise with the average number of trades. I'll start with the simplest version: a 20-day mean of num_trades, which is already unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

The 20-day mean of num_trades gives −0.0025 incremental IC with t = −2.6 and the same sign in every period, so on this history high-trade-volume coins actually lag. Before concluding, I'll check whether the effect is a one-off spike in the 20-day mean by averaging over a longer 60-day window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0326
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0029 (t = -2.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0016, 2023 -0.0023, 2024 -0.0041

The 60-day mean is slightly more negative (−0.0029), so the longer window does not help. One more check on the 20-day mean with min_periods = 16, to see whether the choice of how many days to average matters.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

The 20-day mean with min_periods = 16 is the same as before (−0.0025), so the window choice does not change the result. That is two tests in a row without improving on the first result, so I'll stop here.

What I found: on this history the idea does not hold. Coins with many trades per day went on to underperform slightly, and that holds in every sub-period (2022H2 −0.0013, 2023 −0.0033, 2024 −0.0024), so it is not one bad stretch. I keep the direction the idea states — more trades per day, higher factor — and hand in the 20-day mean of num_trades, which is the simplest form and the one with the most consistent period-by-period numbers.

<factor>Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says a coin whose trade count suddenly jumps far above its own normal level should underperform, so the factor should fall when the trade count rises. I'll start with the simplest form: the 5-day mean of log trade count, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0481
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0089 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0111, 2023 +0.0106, 2024 +0.0062

The first form gives +0.0089 incremental IC with t = 6.1 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history. Next I'll check whether a longer 20-day window is steadier than 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0025 (t = 2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0013, 2023 +0.0033, 2024 +0.0024

The 20-day window is clearly weaker (+0.0025 vs +0.0089), so the signal lives in the recent 5-day jump, not in the 20-day average. One more check on the 5-day window: a 10-day mean instead of a 5-day mean, to see whether a longer average keeps the 5-day direction.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0452
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0065, 2023 +0.0092, 2024 +0.0052

The 10-day average is also weaker (+0.0071), so the 5-day window is the best of the three. I'll stop here rather than spend the last test on a marginal variation.

What I found: negating the 5-day average of the log trade count gives an incremental IC of +0.0089 with t = 6.1, and the sign is the same in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the idea holds on this history — coins whose trade count jumps well above their own 5-day norm go on to do slightly *worse*. The 20-day and 10-day versions both came in below the 5-day one, so the 5-day window is what I hand in.

The idea is about the taker-buy share of quote volume, so I want to measure it as a ratio of USDT volume to total quote volume over a 20-day window (min_periods 16). Higher share, higher factor.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0010
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0102 (t = 3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0190, 2023 +0.0040, 2024 +0.0120

The 20-day taker share gives +0.0102 incremental IC with t = 3.5 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history. Next I want to check whether a shorter 10-day window captures the effect better, since a 5-day window is already a known style.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0028
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0065 (t = 2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0159, 2023 +0.0010, 2024 +0.0074

The 10-day window is clearly weaker (+0.0065, t = 2.2), so the 20-day average is the better one. That's two tests in a row that failed to improve on the first result, so I'll stop and hand in the 20-day version.

What I found: the aggressive-buyer share of quote volume does carry information beyond liquidity, volatility, 1- and 5-day reversal and 30-day momentum. The 20-day average gives +0.0102 incremental IC with t = 3.5, and the sign is the same in 2022H2 (+0.019), 2023 (+0.004) and 2024 (+0.012), so the effect is not a single-period artefact. Shortening the window to 10 days dilutes it, so the 20-day window is the one to keep.

<factor>Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says a coin trading near its recent high is strong and should keep rising, so the factor should rise when the price sits near the recent high. The simplest reading of that is the 5-day high divided by the 5-day low, which is a unit-free ratio, so it is comparable across coins. I'll test that first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0612
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0202 (t = -8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0305, 2023 -0.0164, 2024 -0.0189

The 5-day high/low ratio comes out at −0.0202 with t = −8.7, and every period is negative (−0.031, −0.016, −0.019). So on this history, coins sitting near their recent high actually do slightly worse over the next day. Before concluding, I want to check whether the 5-day window is just a noisy choice: the 20-day high/low is a more persistent "recent high" and is less likely to be a one-day spike.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0111 (t = -6.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0115, 2023 -0.0071, 2024 -0.0149

The 20-day window is less negative (−0.0111, t = −6.2), so the 5-day ratio is the worse of the two. Since the 20-day version is the more stable one, I'll hand that in.

What I found: on this history the idea is not supported — coins sitting near their recent high went on to do slightly *worse* over the next day, and that holds in every sub-period (2022H2 −0.0115, 2023 −0.0071, 2024 −0.0149), so the factor must keep the direction the idea states even though its IC is negative. The 5-day high/low ratio was the first form I tried, and the 20-day one is the better of the two.

The idea is about average daily turnover, so the natural first form is the 20-day mean of `quote_volume / volume` — that is USDT traded per day, which is a cross-coin comparable scale.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0215, 2023 +0.0058, 2024 +0.0092

The 20-day mean of daily turnover gives +0.0103 incremental IC with t = 3.0 and the same sign in all three periods — so the idea holds on this history. Next I check whether a longer 60-day window is steadier.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0080
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0104 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0216, 2023 +0.0059, 2024 +0.0092

The 60-day window gives +0.0104, only 0.0001 above the 20-day one — inside noise, and it is the shorter window that is the simpler expression, so I keep the 20-day version. One more check on the 20-day window with min_periods 16 rather than 16, to see whether the averaging is doing anything.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0071
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0103 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0215, 2023 +0.0058, 2024 +0.0092

The 20-day version with min_periods 16 is exactly the same as the 20-day one (0.0103), so the choice of min_periods does not matter and I stop here.

What I found: coins that trade more per day do outperform over the next days, and the effect survives after removing liquidity, volatility, short-term reversal and 30-day momentum — the 20-day mean of USDT traded per day is the best of the two windows I tried, and it is positive in every sub-period.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('volume')).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says a coin sitting near its recent high is strong and keeps rising, so the factor should rise as the coin's 20-day high rises. I'll start with the simplest version: the 20-day high of close, so the factor is just a ratio of high to close and it is unit-free.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0083 (t = -3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0042, 2023 -0.0065, 2024 -0.0121

The plain 20-day high of close gives incremental IC −0.0083, negative in every sub-period, so on this history coins near their high did worse, not better. Before concluding, I'll check a different reading of "near its recent high": where the close sits inside the 20-day range, which is a bounded, scale-free ratio of high/low.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0067
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0102 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0215, 2023 +0.0055, 2024 +0.0093

The bounded ratio of close to high/low flips the sign to +0.0102 with t = 3.0 and the same sign in all three sub-periods, so the idea does hold in the idea's own direction. That is only 0.0009 above the previous best, so I stop here rather than spend another test.

What I found: the 20-day high of close is a poor signal (−0.0083), but where the close sits inside the 20-day high/low range is a solid one — coins trading near their recent high do outperform, and the effect is positive in 2022H2 (+0.0215), 2023 (+0.0055) and 2024 (+0.0093). The factor is a ratio of close to the 20-day range, so it is comparable across coins and needs no price-level or volume adjustment.

The idea says persistent aggressive selling is bullish, so the factor should rise when the aggressive-buy share of volume has been low for a while. I'll start with the simplest version: a 20-day average of the 1-day taker-buy share, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0010
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0102 (t = -3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0190, 2023 -0.0040, 2024 -0.0120

The 20-day mean of the taker-buy share comes out clearly negative (−0.0102, t = −3.5, negative in all three periods), so on this history coins that have been sold aggressively recently have done worse, the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I want to check whether that is a short-window artefact: a 60-day mean of the same share should show whether the effect is really persistent.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0096
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0143 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0216, 2023 -0.0097, 2024 -0.0153

The 60-day mean is even more negative (−0.0143, t = −4.6, negative in every period), so the effect is not a short-window artefact — the 20-day version is the better of the two and I stop here.

What I found: the aggressive-buy share of volume is a negative signal on this history. Coins that have been sold aggressively over the past 20 days went on to underperform, and that holds in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike (−0.019, −0.004, −0.012), so the idea as stated does not hold here. I keep the direction the idea asks for — a high factor value means persistent aggressive selling — and hand in the 20-day version, which is the least negative of the two.
